upgrade.cABI: Unchanged C ABI, protocol v1, runtime-config v1, public headers and exact e503d27a Swift binding. New local-import v2 commands use the existing generic JSON bus.
upgrade.storageSchema: Explicit physical local-import extension schema2 on base SQLite user_version38; portable snapshot16 and global migration cursor unchanged. Independent reader_local_import_* tables retain local epoch/head, original Applied/Rejected receipts and heavy journals outside portable snapshots and legacy cache cleanup. This is a schema extension, not no-DDL compatibility.
upgrade.terminalDownloadCancel: Completed and Cancelled chapter tasks remain unchanged when a stale or repeated cancel arrives; exact cancel still creates, settles and replays its own receipt without changing a later generation.
upgrade.scope: Extends f3227e30 only with Core-owned current-book source-switch candidate admission and opt-in atomic forward-commit admission. Main Core dirty migrations and later Harmony features are excluded.
upgrade.storageCleanupCompletedRetention: iOS storage summary and cleanup explicitly request retainCompletedQueue; Core inventories current body-complete tasks within the publication guard. Omission retains generic Core cleanup semantics; explicit chapter clear remains destructive.
upgrade.sourceBookDiscovery: Unchanged source-book JSON now skips duplicate SQLite writes; metadata changes use UPDATE, and title changes keep the existing derived-document invalidation trigger. Search acquisition still publishes its own timing/discovery facts.
upgrade.subscriptionPreviewAdmission: iOS sends the complete subscription snapshot and rules mutation head; Core checks both inside the publication guard before replacing the single preview plan. Older callers may omit expected and retain existing Core semantics.
upgrade.downloadResumeAdmission: Retains b5f00c01 request/control-bound expectedResume checks, completed-sibling protection, replay and original ACK semantics.
upgrade.sourceExecutionObservation: runtime.status includeSourceExecution is explicit opt-in; default wire remains closed. Tracks actual queued/running/continuation/callback ownership by requestId and generation, retains bounded retired snapshots, and treats missing/evicted generations as unknown. No C ABI, DDL or cancellation/terminal semantic changes.
upgrade.globalDownloadInventory: cache.download.books.list reads all retained queue states by exact source/book BINARY keyset in one page transaction, including off-shelf/bodyless failures. Bounded metadata and typed media provenance only; no body/TOC/admission/network work, DDL or original write/ACK changes.
upgrade.localImportOriginalReceipts: Authority/persist/publish/finalize/rollback/query/settle v2 bind one epoch/sequence/original transaction and frozen source semantics; business and original positive/negative ACK commit together. Historical query/replay precedes mutable state checks, eight unsettled slots are never evicted, terminal is durable before journal retirement and exact settlement. Legacy unknown outcomes are not promoted into v2.
upgrade.localImportPersistenceMode: Local authority and Host snapshot-only persistence are mutually exclusive under one mode owner; unsupported restore is rejected before business replacement. Generic source IO/commit uncertainty remains Unknown, not a fabricated permanent refusal.
upgrade.sourceSwitchCandidateAdmission: search-book.related mode sourceSwitchCandidates uses exact retained indexed or shelved text identity, existing Core label and author-proof logic, bounded full-row pagination, and current enabled target evidence. New source.switch.commit strictCandidateAdmission=true is checked under the writer after original lineage replay and before mutation; omitted/false retains legacy serialized fingerprints, ACK replay and compensation.
upgrade.sourceSwitchCompatibility: No C ABI, public Swift binding, protocol bus, product version, SQLite base/schema cursor, local import schema2 or portable snapshot generation changes. The new query mode and strict flag require this exact Core. Older strict DTOs cannot interpret new parameters; no downgrade promise is made for newly accepted operations/records. Existing flag-free original operations remain readable and replayable without adopting the new admission policy.
